questions.question: In out-of-order superscalar microarchitectures, what is the primary operational role of the Load-Store Queue (LSQ)?
options: To enable speculative execution of load instructions ahead of older stores while detecting address conflicts and forwarding data from in-flight stores to dependent loads.
To translate virtual page numbers to physical frame numbers before dispatching memory requests to the L1 data cache.
To store retired instructions in strict program order until all architectural registers are updated simultaneously.
To arbitrate bandwidth allocation among concurrent threads sharing a multi-banked L2 cache.
To enforce strict Total Store Order (TSO) by serializing all memory reads and writes through an in-order execution queue.

questions.question: In modern out-of-order processor memory hierarchies, what is the primary architectural purpose of Miss Status Holding Registers (MSHRs) within a cache controller?
options: To maintain a historical table of dirty cache lines scheduled for writeback to DRAM under high bus utilization.
To track outstanding memory requests and their target registers/buffers, allowing the cache to continue serving subsequent hits and misses concurrently.
To predict spatial cache line strides and issue speculative memory prefetches into the L2 cache.
To re-map faulty SRAM cells dynamically using redundant rows and columns during post-fabrication BIST.
To store snooped coherency invalidation requests from neighboring cores until the local pipeline reaches retirement.

questions.question: In Static Timing Analysis (STA) of synchronous digital circuits, why is the hold time timing check fundamentally independent of the operating clock period (T_clk)?
options: Because hold timing violations are masked by clock gating logic prior to the arrival of the active clock edge.
Because hold constraints are calculated exclusively using maximum propagation delays, which cancel out cycle-to-cycle clock jitter.
Because hold timing evaluates whether new data launched by a clock edge prematurely overwrites data captured by that same clock edge, depending only on minimum-delay paths and clock skew.
Because hold time requirements are only enforced during circuit reset and do not apply during active operational cycles.
Because modern EDA tools automatically convert hold time margins into dynamic voltage adjustments during signoff.

questions.question: In semiconductor technology and computer architecture, what physical limitation fundamentally caused the breakdown of classical Dennard scaling in the mid-2000s, triggering the shift toward multi-core microprocessors?
options: Interconnect RC delays exceeding transistor gate delays, preventing further pipeline deepening.
Reaching the quantum tunneling limit of silicon dioxide, which halted further gate width lithography.
Electromigration in copper interconnects reaching critical current density thresholds at sub-micron pitches.
The inability to scale supply voltage (VDD) proportionally with transistor dimensions due to threshold voltage limits and exponentially rising subthreshold leakage power.
The failure of dynamic branch prediction algorithms to scale beyond 4-wide superscalar dispatch widths.

questions.question: In nanoscale CMOS transistor physics and short-channel effect analysis, which statement accurately describes Drain-Induced Barrier Lowering (DIBL)?
options: Excessive gate voltage causes electrons to tunnel directly through the thin gate dielectric into the substrate.
High drain-to-source current creates localized thermal hotspots that degrade electron mobility in the inversion channel.
Impact ionization near the drain junction generates electron-hole pairs, triggering parasitic bipolar latch-up.
Quantum confinement of inversion carriers in ultra-thin nanosheets shifts the conduction band edge away from the Fermi level.
Application of a high drain voltage causes the drain depletion region to penetrate toward the source, lowering the source-channel potential barrier and decreasing the threshold voltage.
